core_obligations: Unwind the hypothesis: write the factorization delta(s) = (1,-1) compose f as the two component identities p d s = f and q d s = -f (source lines 5469-5478).
Define the candidate: set B_n to diamond A_n equal to (p_n, q_n, f_n compose r_n) (source lines 5478-5481).

Check the differential: decompose an element of B_n as a(x_1) + b(x_2) + s(x_3) and verify the compatibility with the differentials term by term, using the two component identities for the third term (source lines 5481-5497).
Conclude uniqueness and compatibility with the splittings, which gives the commutative diagram of the statement (source lines 5497-5504).

proof_roadmap.step: Unwind the factorization into the two component identities and define the map on each degree.
Verify the differential compatibility term by term using the decomposition of an element.
Deduce uniqueness and the compatibility with the splittings.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-map-into-diamond at source lines 5433-5467: for a short exact sequence 0 to A direct sum A to B to C to 0 of chain complexes with termwise splittings s_n whose connecting morphism delta(s) factors through (1,-1) : A[-1] to A[-1] direct sum A[-1], there is a unique morphism B to diamond A making the displayed diagram commute and compatible with the splittings. The proof at source lines 5469-5504 unwinds the factorization into the two component identities p d s = f and q d s = -f, defines the map on B_n as (p_n, q_n, f_n composed with r_n), and then verifies it is a morphism of complexes by writing an arbitrary element as a(x_1) + b(x_2) + s(x_3) and checking the differential compatibility on each of the three terms, the third requiring the two component identities. It is an explicit computation; the substance is the sign pattern and the choice of the third component f r, which is what makes the diagram and the splitting compatibility come out.
